title: Fines for Safety and Screening Violations When Building a House 2026
desc: Fines for building without screening, spilled materials, missing signage or an unposted permit: homeowner and contractor penalties under Decree 339/2026.
summary: The duties on safety, screening, signage and the environment when building a house, and the corresponding fines for homeowners and contractors under the Construction Law 2025 and Decree 339/2026/ND-CP.
body: p

Building in a residential area easily disturbs neighbours: dust, spilled materials, unsafe scaffolding. From 26 August 2026, these violations are fined under Decree 339/2026/ND-CP. This article summarises the duties and fines that homeowners and contractors should know.
h2
1. What must the homeowner do on site?
ul

Install a project signboard at the entrance showing the homeowner's name, address and telephone number; the name and scale of the work; the start and completion dates; and a perspective drawing (Point a, Clause 3, Article 10 of Decree 207/2026/ND-CP; Clause 1, Article 13).
Organise construction and construction supervision and be responsible for safety of the work, neighbouring works and the environment (Point b, Clause 3, Article 10).
Post the content of the construction permit at the construction site (Clause 2, Article 66 of Decree 217/2026/ND-CP).
h2
2. The contractor must ensure safety and environmental hygiene
ul
Fence the site; stack supplies neatly within the site; provide safety instruction signs and fire and explosion prevention signs (Clause 2, Article 13).

Ensure occupational safety and safety for people and vehicles entering and leaving; gather and handle construction waste without adversely affecting the surrounding environment (Clause 3, Article 49 of the Construction Law 2025).
Determine danger zones and prepare safety measures for the project owner's approval; machinery and equipment with strict safety requirements must be inspected before use (Article 51).
Apply environmental protection measures for air, water, solid waste and noise (Article 52).
h2
3. Individuals are fined half
p

The fines in Decree 339/2026/ND-CP are those applicable to organisations; for the same act, an individual is fined half, except for certain acts listed separately (Clause 4, Article 5). A homeowner who is an individual or household, or a builder who is an individual, bears 1/2 of the figures below; a contractor that is a company bears the full amount.
h2
4. Fines for homeowners (detached houses)
ul
Failing to screen, letting materials spill around or placing materials in the wrong place: VND 3–5 million; must screen, clean up and restore the site (Clauses 1 and 14, Article 25).
Not posting the construction permit at the site: VND 5–10 million (Clause 2, Article 25).
Not installing a project signboard or one with missing content: VND 10–20 million (Point b, Clause 1, Article 22).
Building without proper methods or safety, causing subsidence, cracking or damage to neighbouring works: VND 30–40 million (Clause 5, Article 25).
h2
5. Fines for the construction contractor
ul
Failing to screen or letting materials spill when building a detached house: VND 3–5 million (Clause 1, Article 26).
Not stopping work on discovering a risk of occupational accident: VND 10–20 million (Point e, Clause 1, Article 23).
Not determining danger zones; not fully applying construction methods and safety measures: VND 40–60 million (Points g and h, Clause 3, Article 23).
Not stopping work when a work incident or an accident occurs that kills or seriously injures workers; not remedying the consequences: VND 60–80 million (Clause 4, Article 23).
p

Besides fines, violators are ordered to remedy: screen, clean up, install signs, stop work or apply adequate safety measures. The limitation period for fining in the construction sector is 2 years (Article 6).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The fines above apply to detached houses outside heritage and relic areas; other works carry higher levels. Violations of occupational safety and environmental rules may also be handled under other specialised regulations.
